summary: Clinton B. Seely (1936–2021) worked in Indology. He held posts at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he became Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).

Clyde Kluckhohn (1905–1960) studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat (1921–2007) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She served at CNRS, the University of Lyon (1960–1966), Sorbonne Nouvelle (1967–1988), and the Institut de France (~1995–2007).

Colette Sciberras is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.

Colin Mackenzie (1754–1821) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Dollar Academy, he served in the Madras Engineer Group (1786), as Surveyor-General of Madras (1807), and as Surveyor General at the Survey of India (1810–1815).

Colin Turnbull (1924–1994) worked in Tibetology and other fields. He completed his studies at Westminster School (~1939–1942), Magdalen College (~1946–1949), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Collett Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and in Japan at Tokyo and Ryukoku universities. She was appointed professor at the University of Washington in 1985.
Congjun Long works in computational linguistics and Tibetology. Long has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Conor Roddy specializes in philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) under Kathleen Higgins, having also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) studied at Leipzig and Berlin. Specializing in history and archaeology, he held professorships at Leipzig (~1856–1858), Tübingen (~1861–1864), Zurich (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934). He subsequently held a long-term academic appointment at Columbia University (~1946–1979).

Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College and Emory University (PhD 2006–2014 under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock), later holding posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute, Smith College, and Lawrence University.
Constance Powell Chin works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

Constant Chounavel (1825–1923) was active in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Major Seminary of Saint-Dié (~1846–1850) and later served in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Jaffna (1852–1883) and at St. Lucia's Cathedral.

Constantin D. Georgian (1850–1904) was an Indologist and linguist who studied in Bucharest, Paris, and Leipzig. He later taught Romanian at the Academie für moderne Philologie and Sanskrit at the University of Bucharest (1877–1879).

id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
summary: Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney (1757–1820) worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Alexander Hamilton and served as Professor of History at the École Normale Supérieure in ~1795.

Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) studied in Warsaw and Paris. Active in Indology, linguistics, and Tibetology, he held teaching posts at the University of Warsaw (1935, 1937–1939) and professorships at the Universities of Fribourg (1944–1977) and Lausanne (1945–1977).
Constantine Borissoff specializes in linguistics and Indology. Borissoff studied at Far Eastern Federal University, SOAS University of London, and Birkbeck, University of London.

Cora Du Bois (1903–1991) studied at Barnard College and UC Berkeley. She worked for the OSS (~1942–1945) and the State Department (~1945–1949), and held academic posts at Hunter College (~1936–1937) and Harvard University (~1954–1969).
